name: Hungarian Tarokk
description: Hungarian Tarokk (specifically 'Illustrated Tarokk' or 'XX-Hívás Tarokk') is the most popular form of the Tarot family in Hungary. It is a four-player partnership game using the 42-card Austrian/Hungarian Tarot pack. It is highly regarded for its sophisticated system of 'cue-bids' and its unique method of choosing partners by 'calling the XX' (the 20th trump).

history.origins: Part of the Central European Tarot tradition, which arrived in Hungary from Austria in the 19th century.
timeline: 1830s: Tarot games appear in Budapest's coffee houses.
1890s: Modern Hungarian Tarokk rules (with bird imagery/Illustrated) solidify.
1990s: Revival of organized Tarokk clubs in Hungary.
Present: A prestigious strategic game with a dedicated player base.
history.cultural: In Hungary, Tarokk is often calling the 'game of kings' or 'aristocrats', requiring significant mental agility.
history.evolution: The game moved away from scoring purely on points in tricks to a more complex system of bonuses (like 'Pagat Ultimo' and 'XXI Catch').

setup.players: 4 players (2 vs 2 or 3 vs 1 depending on bidding).
setup.deck: 42 cards: 22 Trumps (labeled I to XXI + Skylark/Sküs) and 20 suit cards (King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack and 10/Ace).
setup.dealing: Deal in batches of 6 cards each.

rules.objective: Score game points through contracts and bonuses. The primary goal is usually to win the majority of points in tricks (12 or 16 points).
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit. If unable, MUST play a trump.
2. Standard trick-taking rules: highest trump wins, or highest suit card if no trumps.

strategy.basic: Identify your partner early by observing who plays the XX. Conserve your high trumps to protect your partner's high-value cards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Talon' swap: Use the talon to discard your 'voids' (suits you have none of) so you can trump in on those suits later.
strategy.advanced: Master the cue-bid language. Knowing that your partner has the XIX and the XXI allows you to signal aggressive play styles.
tips: The 'Sküs' is the most powerful card as it is the only one that can 'catch' the XXI.
Keep the lowest trump (I) for the final trick when possible; opponents may force it out earlier.
